documents.title: ResearchTeam
documents.snippet: Conduct rigorous, source-grounded scholarly research with agent-based workflows and robust update safety.
paragraphs: Conduct rigorous, source-grounded scholarly research with agent-based workflows and robust update safety.
**Documentation:** https://jlcatonjr.github.io/researchteam/ · **API Reference:** https://jlcatonjr.github.io/researchteam/api-reference/

ResearchTeam is a pip-installable framework for producing well-structured research reports with verified citations, using agent-based workflows. All claims are grounded in peer-reviewed or reputable scholarly sources, with Chicago-style citations. Once installed, a derived project can receive infrastructure updates automatically — without touching user research content.
```bash pip install "researchteam @ git+https://github.com/jlcatonjr/researchteam.git@v1.0.2" ```

Install the latest signed `v1.0.N` tag (currently `v1.0.2`); for a verified install from a separate tag checkout, see [`docs/CONTRIBUTING.md`](docs/CONTRIBUTING.md). `release/1.0` holds reviewed fixes queued for the next patch release: unsigned between tags, not for pinning. How branches, releases and contributions work: [`docs/CONTRIBUTING.md`](docs/CONTRIBUTING.md).
`init` scaffolds a complete project directory, seeds a neutral placeholder `brief.json`, generates a project-specific `README.md` / `CLAUDE.md`, runs `git init`, and makes an initial commit. Then:

1. Edit `brief.json` to describe your project (name, goal, `layer2_profile`, etc.). 2. Run `researchteam personalize` to regenerate `README.md` and `CLAUDE.md`'s header from the updated `brief.json`. 3. Run `researchteam materialize` to re-render the agent team so agent bodies reflect your project's domain and identity.
```bash git clone https://github.com/jlcatonjr/researchteam.git my-research-project cd my-research-project ```
Then follow the onboarding steps in `CLAUDE.md` or `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.
``` researchteam init [name] [--ref REF] [--remote URL] [--vulnscan-level off|scan] ```

- `name` — directory to create (defaults to current directory if empty) - `--ref` — upstream git ref to scaffold from (default: `main`) - `--remote` — git remote URL to set as `origin` after init - `--vulnscan-level` — set `brief.json`'s `vulnerability_scanning.level` (default `scan`, from the scaffold); `remediate` is an operator choice via `agentteams --set-vulnscan`
``` researchteam update [--yes] [--dry-run] [--layer2-only | --layer1-only] [--ref REF] [--accept-upstream PATH] [--no-codex] ```

- `--yes / -y` — skip interactive confirmation; required in CI - `--dry-run` — show what would change without writing files - `--layer2-only` — only sync layer-2 files; skip `agentteams --update --merge` - `--ref` — override the upstream ref (default: the release-locked `toolchain.lock`'s verified researchteam tag, else the `.researchteam` marker, else `main`) - `--accept-upstream PATH` — take upstream's part above `## Project-Specific Notes` of an `above-notes` file the repo
ResearchTeam infrastructure is split into two independently updatable layers:
**User-owned files** (`brief.json`, `Projects/`, `references/`) are never touched by any update layer.

`README.md` and `CLAUDE.md`'s header are **generated per-project** from `brief.json`, not synced from upstream — `researchteam update` never re-imposes the framework's own identity on them. Regenerate them with `researchteam personalize`. `CLAUDE.md` is dual-managed: its title and *Project Purpose* header are project-owned/generated, while the fenced-preserve `researchteam:managed` block carries synced framework governance.
`researchteam update` (without `--layer2-only`) runs both update layers in sequence. See `docs/researchteam-framework.md` for the full model.

Projects created with `researchteam init` receive a `.github/workflows/agentteams-sync.yml` that runs both layers on `workflow_dispatch`. Its weekly schedule ships commented out (#186): turning it on is a deliberate edit in the project, and `researchteam workflow-sync` (which with `--workflow validate` also adds an opt-in, read-only validate workflow) keeps that choice when it updates the workflow. The CI:

1. Installs the `researchteam` CLI (verifying a release-locked tag first) 2. Runs `scripts/agentteams_autosync_gate.sh --mode derived`: SHA gate, pinned `agentteams` install, full `researchteam update`, blocking gates 3. Validates changed paths and fence integrity 4. On a change, opens or updates one evergreen PR (`chore/agentteams-autosync`) for human review; a manual run with `force=true` integrates even when the agentteams SHA is unchanged

The orchestrator agent is the entry point for all agent-based workflows. It coordinates requests, enforces constitutional rules, and ensures every multi-file session closes with a consistency check. **Do not bypass the orchestrator or invoke agents directly, except for the Team Builder bootstrap flow.**

documents.snippet: The `researchteam` console script (`researchteam.cli:main`). Every subcommand and flag below is defined in [`researchteam/cli.py`](https://github.com/jlcatonjr/researchteam/blob/main/researchteam/cli.py); the test suite fails if this page a
paragraphs: The `researchteam` console script (`researchteam.cli:main`). Every subcommand and flag below is defined in [`researchteam/cli.py`](https://github.com/jlcatonjr/researchteam/blob/main/researchteam/cli.py); the test suite fails if this page and the parser drift apart.

`update`, `personalize` and `materialize` run only inside a derived repo (they walk up from the current directory for a `.researchteam` marker and exit 1 without one). `status` and `doctor` also work in the upstream repo.
``` researchteam init [name] [--ref REF] [--remote URL] [--vulnscan-level off|scan] [--adopt] ```
``` researchteam update [--yes] [--dry-run] [--layer2-only | --layer1-only] [--ref REF] [--accept-upstream PATH]... [--no-codex] ```
When `toolchain.lock` release-locks researchteam but its tag does not verify, `update` refuses (fail closed; it never falls back to `main`). Pass `--ref` to choose a ref deliberately.

The resolved ref must be a plain branch, tag or commit name; otherwise `update` exits 1 with a message naming the ref, before fetching anything. A commit ref (other than the verified release-locked one) must be on researchteam's `main` or a `release/*` branch, because GitHub serves a fork's commits under this repository's URL too: `update` refuses a commit GitHub says is on neither, and warns and continues when GitHub cannot answer (offline or rate-limited; a `GITHUB_TOKEN` r
Refuses in the upstream repository (`is_upstream = true` in `.researchteam`). Implementation: [`personalize`](api-reference/personalize.md).
``` researchteam materialize [--yes] [--dry-run] [--copilot-only] [--adopt-orphans] [--discard-user-regions] [--no-codex] ```

Plain `update` merges with `--shrink-policy preserve` and will not re-brand enriched agent bodies; use `materialize` after a domain or identity change in `brief.json`. Implementation: [`update`](api-reference/update.md) (`run_materialize`).

documents.title: Getting Started
documents.snippet: `researchteam` is the entry point. `agentteams` is installed **through it as an extra**, never on its own: it is not published to PyPI, so the base install declares no dependencies and a bare install leaves layer-1 agent regeneration unavai
paragraphs: `researchteam` is the entry point. `agentteams` is installed **through it as an extra**, never on its own: it is not published to PyPI, so the base install declares no dependencies and a bare install leaves layer-1 agent regeneration unavailable.
```bash pip install "researchteam @ git+https://github.com/jlcatonjr/researchteam.git@v1.0.2"
pip install "researchteam[update] @ git+https://github.com/jlcatonjr/researchteam.git@v1.0.2"
pip install "researchteam[research] @ git+https://github.com/jlcatonjr/researchteam.git@v1.0.2" ```

These install the signed `v1.0.2` tag. For a verified install (a separate checkout of the tag, its signature checked with repository config neutralised), see [`docs/CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/jlcatonjr/researchteam/blob/main/docs/CONTRIBUTING.md).
Check that both tools resolve in the **active** interpreter:
```bash python -m pip show researchteam agentteams researchteam doctor ```
`init` scaffolds a complete project directory, seeds a neutral placeholder `brief.json`, generates a project-specific `README.md` / `CLAUDE.md`, runs `git init`, and makes an initial commit. Then:

1. Edit `brief.json` to describe your project (name, goal, `layer2_profile`, components, …). 2. Run `researchteam personalize` to regenerate `README.md` and `CLAUDE.md`'s header from the brief. 3. Run `researchteam materialize` to re-render the agent team so agent bodies reflect your domain and identity. 4. Choose your workflow: Claude (`CLAUDE.md`) or Copilot (`.github/copilot-instructions.md`). 5. Run `bash scripts/claude_researchteam_bridge.sh validate`.
```bash researchteam update            # interactive — shows a diff for each changed file researchteam update --yes      # non-interactive (CI) researchteam update --dry-run  # preview only ```

Projects created with `init` also receive `.github/workflows/agentteams-sync.yml`, which runs on `workflow_dispatch` (its weekly Monday 06:00 UTC schedule ships commented out; uncommenting it is a deliberate choice, #186), gated on the agentteams commit, and opens one evergreen PR running both layers when agentteams changed (a manual run with `force` skips the gate).
`toolchain.lock` records the researchteam and agentteams commits a derived repo was last synced and verified with. To run exactly that pair:

```bash bash scripts/bootstrap_toolchain.sh          # .venv with the pinned commits (gitignored) python3 scripts/check_toolchain.py           # installed vs toolchain.lock vs upstream main (not for release-locked pins) ```
See [`scripts`](api-reference/scripts.md) for `check_toolchain.py`'s flags and the lock format.

documents.title: ResearchTeam
documents.snippet: Conduct rigorous, source-grounded scholarly research with agent-based workflows and updates that never touch your research content.
paragraphs: Conduct rigorous, source-grounded scholarly research with agent-based workflows and updates that never touch your research content.

`researchteam` is a pip-installable framework that scaffolds and maintains an agent-based research project: a team of governance and domain agents (generated from `brief.json` by the companion [`agentteams`](https://jlcatonjr.github.io/agentteams/) tool), plus the docs, scripts, and checklists that support them. Deliverables are Markdown research reports with Chicago-style citations, every claim traceable to a scholarly source.

A derived repository describes **its own project**. The framework keeps the shared infrastructure current without touching your research content: `brief.json`, `Projects/` and `references/` are never written by an update.
```bash pip install "researchteam[update] @ git+https://github.com/jlcatonjr/researchteam.git@v1.0.2" ```
```bash researchteam init my-research-project cd my-research-project researchteam doctor ```
See [Getting Started](getting-started.md) for the other install variants and the onboarding steps.

documents.snippet: **Week:** 2026-W36 · **Date:** 2026-08-31 · **Owner:** orchestrator session **Source spec:** `docs/gitignore-preservation-handoff.md` (v1.1, adversarially audited 2026-08-26)
paragraphs: **Week:** 2026-W36 · **Date:** 2026-08-31 · **Owner:** orchestrator session **Source spec:** `docs/gitignore-preservation-handoff.md` (v1.1, adversarially audited 2026-08-26)

`.gitignore` is a `MANAGED_FILES` entry; layer-2 sync (`_update_cmd.py`) overwrites every managed file wholesale from upstream. Any ignore pattern that exists only in a derived repo is silently deleted on the next `researchteam update --yes` (the blind weekly CI path), turning correctly ignored files into stageable ones. Root-cause fix requested by the SocialScienceHumanities session.

Per-file merge strategy. `.gitignore` opts into `fenced-preserve`: upstream owns a comment-fenced managed block; everything outside the fence is preserved verbatim across syncs. Default strategy stays `overwrite`, so no other managed file changes behavior. Layer-2 only; no agentteams change.

1. Derived lines survive `--yes` (fenced local). 2. Upstream additions inside the fence land. 3. Upstream removals inside the fence apply. 4. No spurious deletions in preview (diff computed against fenced region only). 5. Pre-fence migration is non-destructive (diverged unfenced local never silently wiped under `--yes`). 6. Other managed files unchanged (overwrite default; `.sh` exec bit preserved). 7. Idempotent (identical managed block → no write).

- Backwards compatible: `MERGE_STRATEGIES` defaults to `overwrite`. - Degrade-safe: if upstream copy is unfenced, `fenced-preserve` refuses to wholesale-overwrite (keeps local + warns) rather than reintroducing the loss. - One upstream edit: wrap this repo's `.gitignore` body in the fence markers. - PR #9 merge is independent (separate commit already reviewed).

documents.title: Fix: the release-line candidate from a stable lock must be stable (researchteam 1.1.1)
documents.snippet: Reported by infrastructureManagement on 2026-11-09 (agentteams row 691; agentteams-6c verified it in source).
paragraphs: Reported by infrastructureManagement on 2026-11-09 (agentteams row 691; agentteams-6c verified it in source).

**Defect.** `researchteam._release.newest_on_line` keeps every tag on the line with `tag_key > current`. Because `tag_key` orders `v1.1.1-rc.1` above `v1.1.0`, a STABLE lock gets an rc as its candidate. `check_toolchain.py --release-candidate` then prints it, and the autosync gate integrates it. baseAgent #324 (v1.1.0 → v1.1.1-rc.1) shows this. It breaks the latest-stable rule: adopting an rc requires a recorded `@security` clearance.

**Fix.** - `newest_on_line(repo, current, include_prerelease=None)`: from a stable `current`, only stable tags are eligible. From an rc, newer rcs and the final stay eligible. `include_prerelease=True` is an explicit opt-in. - `check_toolchain.py --release-candidate NAME [--include-prerelease]`. The autosync gate never passes the flag. - `--write-lock --tag name=<rc>` is unchanged: a deliberate rc pin is still possible, with its own signed row.
**Tests:** stable→rc refused, stable→stable, rc→final, rc→rc, the opt-in, and the existing line tests.

**Release.** researchteam v1.1.1, a patch on release/1.1: PR to main, then the operator fast-forwards release/1.1 and signs v1.1.1. Derived repos move with `--researchteam-tag v1.1.1`, which re-syncs check_toolchain.py and installs the fixed `_release.py`. Until they do, keep autosync held for v1.1-locked repos.

documents.title: P1 step 0.3: copy-integrity design for the term-index core (design note, 2026-11-20)
documents.snippet: **Recommendation.** Copy the upstream core files byte-identically into `scripts/term-index-core/`, with a `PINNED.json` manifest of sha256 values beside them. One stdlib-only script, `scripts/check_term_core.py`, checks the files against th
paragraphs: **Recommendation.** Copy the upstream core files byte-identically into `scripts/term-index-core/`, with a `PINNED.json` manifest of sha256 values beside them. One stdlib-only script, `scripts/check_term_core.py`, checks the files against the manifest without network access, and loads them under a private package name. The term index never imports an installed agentteams. CI proves that the copy matches the manifest. Proof that the manifest matches the signed agentteams tag co

Plan: `references/plans/open-1119-p1-term-index-core-switch.plan.md`. Option C and the 1.3.0 placement are operator rulings and are not re-decided here. All upstream facts below come from agentteams `dev` at `b4b732f`, which is unreleased and provisional.

At `b4b732f` the core is two files. `term_index.py` line 37 reads `from agentteams._term_text import (...)`, and `_term_text.py` imports only `bisect` and `re`. A byte-identical copy cannot rewrite that import.
**Decision: the design assumes (b), because only (b) works with the code as it stands. It is built so that (a) or (c) only removes the shim step.** The same loader handles all three:

- It reads `PINNED.json` and reads each listed file's bytes once. - It checks each hash and compiles the bytes it checked, so nothing changes between the check and the load. - It creates a private package `_researchteam_term_core` with an empty `__path__`, so nothing is found on disk. Each file becomes a submodule of that package, registered in `sys.modules` before it runs. The `@dataclass` classes in `term_index.py` need that registration. - Files load in manifest order. The

**The shim, for (b) only.** The loader saves whatever is at `sys.modules["agentteams._term_text"]`, or notes that the key is absent. It puts the pinned `_term_text` there, runs `term_index.py`, and then restores the saved value or deletes the key in a `finally` block.

In CPython, `from agentteams._term_text import ...` returns the module already in `sys.modules` without importing the parent `agentteams` package, so an installed agentteams is never loaded. A probe on 2026-11-20 with the two `b4b732f` files confirmed this on Python 3.13 and 3.14, with and without an importable agentteams: the parent package was not imported and `term_index.Matcher` was the pinned object. Python 3.10 was not available to the probe; the L1 test in section 5 co

After loading, the core's globals point directly at the pinned objects. The loader checks `term_index.Matcher is <pinned _term_text>.Matcher` with an explicit `raise`, not an `assert`, so `python -O` cannot remove it.

**Directory.** The directory is `scripts/term-index-core/`. Its name is not a valid Python identifier, so a normal `import` can never reach these files, even with `scripts/` on `sys.path`. Each file is added to `SCHOLARLY_MANAGED_FILES` in `researchteam/_manifest.py`. Layer-2 sync fetches each listed file one at a time from the researchteam ref, which is a verified tag's peeled commit when the repository is release-locked. A derived repository therefore receives the copy only
**Decision: in `scripts/term-index-core/PINNED.json`, synced by the same list, so a copy and its hashes always come from the same researchteam commit.**

```json {"format": "researchteam-pinned-copy/1", "upstream": {"repository": "jlcatonjr/agentteams", "tag": "v1.3.x", "commit": "<40-hex peeled>"}, "entry": "term_index", "files": [{"upstream_path": "agentteams/_term_text.py", "local_path": "scripts/term-index-core/_term_text.py", "sha256": "<64-hex>"}, ...]} ```
Local paths must sit inside the directory: no `..`, no absolute paths, no symbolic links.

The hashes are not in `toolchain.lock`, for three reasons: - The lock is repository-owned and never synced, so its hash would drift from the synced copy. - A derived repository may pin a different agentteams patch, and its autosync rewrites the lock. - The lock records what the toolchain was verified with. The manifest records where the copied bytes came from.
**Decision: `scripts/check_term_core.py`.** It is both the command and the loader the adapters import, so they share one hash routine. It imports no network module and never fetches.

- **Output:** one line per file (`[term-core] OK <path>` or `[term-core] MISMATCH <path>: sha256 <12 hex>, expected <12 hex> (agentteams <tag> <upstream_path>)`), then a summary line naming the tag, the short commit and the counts. - **Exit 0:** every file matches. - **Exit 1:** a file is mismatched, missing or a symbolic link, or a `.py` file in the directory is not listed in the manifest. - **Exit 2:** the manifest is unreadable or malformed.

**Where it runs:** - **Bridge `validate`:** `run_term_index_check` runs the core check first. Its "both files or neither" presence test is extended to cover the core directory. - **`term-build`, `term-check` and `term-query`:** these run it implicitly at import. A failure exits 2 and prints the check's lines. - **The edit hook:** it writes nothing and reports the failure. - **An optional bridge command, `term-core-check`.**

Cost does not decide where it runs. Hashing two files of tens of kilobytes takes well under a millisecond, which is negligible beside a scan. Checking at import is what makes the mechanism fail closed. There is no override, and `TERM_INDEX_ADVISORY` does not soften it. To repair a failure, run `git checkout` on the directory, or `researchteam update` with a researchteam that knows the directory (section 10, point 1).

A new `_check_term_core(root, ok, warn, fail)` follows `_check_toolchain`: - It runs the script under `sys.executable` with a timeout, passes each line through `_printable`, and relays it. - It stays silent where the gate script is absent. `_check_scholarly_tooling` already reports that, and the manifest is added to its list.

**Decision: a mismatch is `[FAIL]`, unlike the informational term-index check.** It means the code that runs is not the code researchteam shipped, which is the same class of problem as "agentteams installed but not runnable". This is listed as an open question.

There are two `ok` lines: the pinned tag and commit, and "the term index uses the pinned copy, never the installed agentteams". If the manifest tag and the lock's `agentteams.tag` are on different `vX.Y` lines, doctor prints a `warn`.

The engine's matching, masking, form keys and generated-file layout match upstream line for line, once `TermIndexConfig` and the function arguments carry researchteam's values. The main blocker is that upstream `term_index.py` imports `agentteams._term_text`, so a byte-identical copy under `scripts/` cannot be imported without the `agentteams` package. Separately, three behaviour points have no upstream parameter or counterpart; they are listed first under "Gaps and differenc

Sources read: - `scripts/term_index_engine.py` (674 lines) - `scripts/build_term_index.py`, `check_term_index.py` and `query_term_index.py` (the actual caller names) - `references/plans/open-1119-p1-term-index-core-switch.plan.md` - The two upstream copies: `agentteams `dev` at `b4b732f`: term_index.py` and `agentteams `dev` at `b4b732f`: _term_text.py`
Abbreviations: "TI" means upstream `term_index.py` and "TT" means upstream `_term_text.py`. "Cfg.x" means the `TermIndexConfig` field `x` (TI:143-171).

1. **Upstream cannot be copied as a standalone file.** TI:37-39 reads: ```python from agentteams._term_text import ( WORD, Matcher, form_key, form_keys, glob_match, lead_key, mask, match_words, quoted_spans, term_forms, ) ``` This is an absolute, package-qualified import of a private module. - **Without `agentteams` installed:** a byte-identical `term_index.py` under `scripts/` cannot be imported as-is. The import at line 37 raises `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'agent

2. **NOREG hint text has no parameter.** - Engine (`check_term_index.py:154`): `"its terms.json is not a researchteam register"` / `"run: term-init"`. Upstream (TI:700): `"its terms.json has no accepted schema marker"` / `"add terms.json"`. - The gate code (NOREG) and the exit code are unchanged; the printed line changes. - Verified by reading both.

3. **`manifest_matches` and `manifest_is_current` have no upstream counterpart.** These are engine lines 599 and 604; the hook uses them at `build_term_index.py:217`. The generator and register-hash test is inline at TI:570. The adapter would have to keep its own copy, built from `load_register`, `read_manifest`, `documents` and `read_document`, and pass `config.generator`. This is core logic that would stay outside the pinned copy. Verified.

4. **Upstream defaults are neutral, so any call that omits the config or `is_project` changes results.** Verified by reading both sides. - (a) `skip_heading=None`: References/Bibliography sections get scanned, so new occurrences and different `index/*.json` bytes. With an unchanged generator string that is STALE "differs from a fresh build"; with a different one it is REBUILD. - (b) `is_project=None` makes `documents()` skip only folders holding a register (TI:392, 412). The

5. **Message for an oversized register.** - Engine:236: `"terms.json is larger than 1000000 bytes"`. Upstream TI:354-355: `"terms.json is a link, not a regular file, or larger than 1000000 bytes (refused)"`. - Same code (SCHEMA) and status (BAD). - Verified.

6. **Symbolic-link handling on read-back is stricter upstream. This can make a clean project fail.** - Engine: `_generated_file_problems` (`check_term_index.py:84-86`) checks only the last path component (`is_symlink()`) and then `read_bytes()`, which follows links in parent directories. `stray_index_files` returns an empty set when `terminology/index` is a link (engine:671). - Upstream: `_freshness` reads through `read_capped` (TI:639), which opens every component with `O_NO

7. **Capped read of generated files.** - Upstream `_read_json` refuses committed JSON over `MAX_GENERATED_BYTES` = 20,000,000 (TI:59, 515). A manifest that large would become "no usable index manifest" (STALE). - The engine reads it uncapped (engine:588). - `_freshness` caps each comparison at the expected length (TI:639); the outcome is the same as the engine's byte comparison. - Verified by reading. Not reachable for realistic projects.

8. **Document and register reads (race-only differences).** - **Missing file:** upstream `read_document` turns `FileNotFoundError` into `None`, which becomes a SCOPE defect (TI:446-447, exit 1). In the engine, `lstat` raises, which is exit 2 in check (`check_term_index.py:219`) and in build (`build_term_index.py:255`). This only happens if a file disappears between the walk and the read. - **Growing file:** upstream reads at most cap+1 bytes through the open descriptor and re

9. **Upstream does things the engine does not, and none of them changes a stable, link-free project.** Verified. - Per-component `O_NOFOLLOW` with `dir_fd` (TI:61-62, 91-99), `O_NONBLOCK`, `fstat`, capped reads (TI:65-132). - Accepts the neutral schema. - `region_filter` (unused, defaults to `None`). - `register_text_problems` split out. - `check_project`, `_freshness` and `_usage` moved into the core. - Effects on currently clean projects are limited to items 6 and 7.

10. **No difference found (verified line by line).** - `Matcher` (`__init__`, `_pattern`, `_hits`, `occurrences`); TT adds only `skip_heading`. - `mask` (only `in_refs` becomes `in_skip`), `quoted_spans`, `_paragraph_quotes`, `_code_spans`. - `form_key`, `form_keys`, `match_words`, `lead_key`, `glob_match`. - All validation messages and limits. - STALE / REBUILD / DISC / NOSRC / UNUSED / QUOTED / ORPHAN text, with `rebuild_hint="term-build"`.
11. **Status note.** The TI docstring (TI:3) calls the module "beta (outside SemVer in 1.3.x)". A pinned copy guards bytes, but the API may change between 1.3.x releases.

12. **The plan's state section is out of date** (TV-07): ``` [TV-07] references/plans/open-1119-p1-term-index-core-switch.plan.md:17 Expected (in source): agentteams/term_index.py exists on dev (commit b4b732f, per the caller) Found (in deliverable): "`agentteams/term_index.py` does not exist on `dev`." Authority source: caller statement; a scratch copy of the upstream term_index.py Recommended action: update the dated state line when the plan is next revised ```

paragraphs: Written 2026-11-19 by the researchteam agent session, for the agent that takes this over.
The next release tag (1.2.1 or 1.3.0) shows GitHub's "Verified" badge, and the cut script proves it.

- `v1.1.9`, `v1.2.0-rc.1` and `v1.2.0` all report `verified=false`, reason **`unknown_key`**. - All three verify against the release key with `scripts/check_toolchain.py --verify-tag`. The signatures are good; only GitHub's display is affected. - **Cause found.** The account's public key lists show the release key (fingerprint ending `…qxnzTNM`) registered as an **authentication** key only. The one **signing** key on the account is a different key. GitHub therefore cannot mat
(a) the signing key registered on the tagger's account as a **signing** key, and (b) a tagger email that is a verified address of that account. (a) is unmet today. (b) is not yet checked.

1. **Check condition (b), read-only.** Read the tagger email of `v1.2.0` from the tag object and say whether it can be a verified address of the account. Do not print a personal address into any tracked file. 2. **Operator decisions.** Two were answered in the authoring session's picker on 2026-11-19: - **Signing key: "Prepare the script".** The next agent writes and hands over the registration script (step 3). The answer covers preparing the script; running it is the operato

One remains for Gate 1: confirm "fix forward only: the existing tags stay". The options as first put: - Register the release key as a signing key on the GitHub account? It is an account setting, so the operator does it; the agent prepares a script with one command (PS-3), reviewed by `@security`. The script reads the public key only and prints its fingerprint. - Which tagger email? Recommended: the account's GitHub-provided no-reply address. GitHub always treats it as verifie

documents.snippet: Evidence gathered by the orchestrator the same day: setting `delete_branch_on_merge` is `false`; rulesets forbid deleting `main`, `release/**` and `archive/**` with no bypass; no workflow, lock or tracked link names a short-lived branch oth
paragraphs: Evidence gathered by the orchestrator the same day: setting `delete_branch_on_merge` is `false`; rulesets forbid deleting `main`, `release/**` and `archive/**` with no bypass; no workflow, lock or tracked link names a short-lived branch other than the evergreen autosync branch.
**Verdict: SAFE WITH CONDITIONS.** The setting is technically safe. The governance case is not: amending PS-2 is necessary but does not by itself satisfy C-5 or the fenced text.

**1. Autosync. The plan's claim is true.** - After a merge, the `evergreen_pr` job finds no open PR (`agentteams-sync.yml:47-50`). The `git show origin/chore/agentteams-autosync:…` probe fails, so the evergreen branch is never consulted (`agentteams_autosync_gate.sh:173`). The baseline then comes from main's own `.github/agentteams-autosync-ref` (`:185-187`), which the merge just updated. - A sync that is still needed is not skipped and nothing loops. Equal SHAs exit with no

**2. Other dependencies on a merged branch surviving.** None are live. - Release cuts fast-forward `release/*` from the merge commit on main (`references/plans/archive/2026-W47/operator/19-cut-v1.2.1.sh:92-123`). - `PIN_BRANCH` is `main` (`archive/2026-W42/operator/common.sh:28`). - Rulesets already protect `archive/**`, so PS-1 is not affected. - Two residual risks remain: - **Stacked PRs.** They have been used here (`archive/2026-W42/operator/04-merge-prs.sh:54`). GitHub wo

**3. Governance.** - PS-2 text that A contradicts (`.claude/CLAUDE.md:391-393`): "Deletions still follow S-4 and need the operator's explicit confirmation. Remote branch deletion needs the operator's signed `branch-delete` grant or a recorded `@security` `--branch-cleanup` PASS. PS-2 replaces neither." - **There is fenced text the amendment cannot reach.** - `branch-lifecycle.reference.md` §3 guard 8 (`:88`) says every deletion is recorded in the ledger. §5 (`:172-174`) recom

**Conditions for A:** 1. Before the setting changes, `@security` records a decision row such as `repo-setting:delete_branch_on_merge`. It is scoped to PR head refs in this repository, carries a sunset and a cap slot, and ends on a HALT on `branch-delete`. 2. The PS-2 amendment states honestly that: - GitHub deletes the head of any merged PR, whatever its base; - no ledger row is written; - no hold checks run (owner, link, worktree, session, retargeting of dependent PRs); - re

**For the operator:** A is technically safe, autosync included. But it means permanently giving up the deletion record and the hold checks, and to stay inside C-5 it needs a recorded `@security` clearance that expires and takes a cap slot, not just a PS-2 edit. B costs a reviewed script every week or two and changes no rule. Choose A only if that periodic review no longer earns its cost.

The test then signs a decision row and checks the gate's refusal wording against that arbitrary version. On 2026-11-19 that checkout was moving toward `v1.2.1`. In the `at` runs here the

documents.snippet: I read the plan first: `references/plans/open-1119-p4-unreproduced-test-failure.plan.md`. I wrote no files.
paragraphs: I read the plan first: `references/plans/open-1119-p4-unreproduced-test-failure.plan.md`. I wrote no files.

**What I read.** - **Read in full:** `conftest.py`, `test_agentteams_provenance.py`, `test_release_lock.py`, `test_toolchain.py`, `test_scaffold_fixes.py`, `test_reviewed_commit.py`, `test_frozen_surfaces.py`, `test_drift.py`, `test_init_fetch.py`, `test_sign_key.py`, `test_trust_root_step.py`, `test_derived_workflow.py`, `test_conflict_log.py`, `test_autosync_no_pr_alert.py`, `test_doctor_informational.py`, `test_bridge_validate_hooks.py`, `test_version.py`, `test_module_ent

**One of the facts you gave does not hold.** No test file inserts the repository root into `sys.path`. - Only `scripts/` gets inserted: permanently by `test_bibliography_explorer.py:21`, and temporarily (restored) by `test_term_index.py:33-48`. - `tests/` is on `sys.path` only through pytest's default prepend mode. `test_reviewed_commit.py:86` depends on that. - So which `researchteam` gets imported depends on how pytest is started: - `python -m pytest` run from the repositor

- `test_init_signing_steps.py` - `test_library_query_args.py` (only seen through searches; it loads a script by path) - `test_marker_reader.py` (only seen through searches; its one `chdir` is restored by monkeypatch)

Risk marks: **HIGH** = not isolated and can fail from machine state or timing; **MED** = isolated except for one plausible leak, or fails only if a specific variable is set; **LOW** = isolated, or the leak cannot change the result.

It is `tests/test_scaffold_fixes.py:36`, `test_signer_appends_verified_row`. It is the only test that calls `pytest.importorskip("agentteams")`. A second test, `test_frozen_surfaces.py:238`, is gated by an environment variable rather than by agentteams being present.
When agentteams **is** importable at a version other than the lock's pin, the test runs instead of skipping:

1. It runs `scripts/sign_security_decision.py --action overwrite --conditions test` as a subprocess under `sys.executable`, in a temporary workspace. - Only `AGENTTEAMS_DECISION_SIGNING_KEY` is replaced, with a 39-byte throwaway key. Every other `AGENTTEAMS_*` variable from the session is inherited. - The script imports `agentteams.cli.decision_log.sign_decision_row` and `agentteams.cli.security_gate.check_clearance` from that arbitrary version. - It appends an HMAC-signed PA

It fails if that version: - lacks either function (the script exits 1 with "agentteams is not importable"), or - rejects the row, for example over author rules, the key or placeholder rules, a hash-chained log or required columns (the script rolls back and exits 1), or - words the refusal differently. The local checkout today says "…failed signature verification", which matches.
**Unverified:** whether any given agentteams version's `check_clearance` reads home-directory config.
In CI, and under `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3`, the test is skipped. That fits a failure that showed once and never came back.

1. **`test_scaffold_fixes.py:36` (hypotheses 2 and 5).** - **Would fail if:** the run used the other repository's virtualenv, where agentteams is an editable install of the local checkout on whatever branch it had then (around PR #214), and that code's signer or gate API, its acceptance of the row, or its refusal wording differed. - Every later run in CI or under Homebrew's python skips this test, so it would never fail again. 2. **`test_notes.py:156` (one per agent) and `tes

**Environment-variable cases (hypothesis 4).** These fail only if the session exported the variable, and most would fail in groups rather than alone: - `RESEARCHTEAM_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED_AGENTTEAMS=1`: 3 provenance params fail. - `RT_TEST_AGENTTEAMS_PYTHON`: the frozen-surfaces test at :238 fails. - `AUTOSYNC_PR_BODY_FILE`: 4 gate tests fail. - `RT_ROOT`: 2 bridge tests fail. - A proxy without `no_proxy` covering 127.0.0.1: 5 reviewed-commit tests fail.

**Hypothesis 3 (network timeout or rate limit) has no viable candidate.** The GitHub API is pinned to `127.0.0.1:9`. Every ls-remote or fetch is patched or shimmed. The one real request (item 5) catches its own errors.

**The stale-researchteam half of hypothesis 5 is unlikely.** Importing an installed researchteam instead of the checkout would cause many failures or collection errors, not one. The only tests that would single it out are `test_workflow_sync.py:54` and :236.

**The release signers file.** No test needs the real `~/.config/agentteams/allowed_signers`. Every path that could read it is overridden: - `_release.allowed_signers_path` reads `AGENTTEAMS_ALLOWED_SIGNERS`, which fixtures set; `test_release_lock.py:97` points it at a missing file on purpose. - The gate's `$HOME` fallback is never reached: `_gate_group_run` sets the variable at :490, and the install-gate runs exit before that point. - The derived-workflow tests remove or set

So a scratch HOME makes no test fail or skip because of the signers file. Two caveats I could not check: - A scratch HOME also removes the global git config and excludes file. documents.snippet: **Date:** 2026-11-16 **Trigger (operator request):** every researchteam project should define its terms in a coded register so that consistent usage can be enforced; every appearance of a listed term across project documentation should be i
paragraphs: **Date:** 2026-11-16 **Trigger (operator request):** every researchteam project should define its terms in a coded register so that consistent usage can be enforced; every appearance of a listed term across project documentation should be indexed; and the index should be kept in sync by a hook or a similarly reliable trigger. **Research basis:** `Projects/CodedTermIndexing/` (literature review, analysis section 7, conclusion). **Status:** REVISED after audit and IMPLEMENTED.
The draft was audited by `@adversarial`, `@conflict-auditor`, `@security` and `@code-hygiene`. The adversarial verdict was RETHINK. The resolutions below are binding.

- **R1. The draft did not enforce usage (adversarial F-1, F-17).** Every blocking check in the draft concerned the register or the index. The one check on usage, a discouraged form in prose, was advisory. The research infers, as a judgement and not an established finding, that a register nothing checks usage against should not be expected to produce consistent usage. → A discouraged form outside a quotation, with no recorded exception, is a blocking `DEFECT[DISC]`. A delibera

The first implementation (commit 761c938) was reviewed by `@security`, `@code-hygiene` and `@conflict-auditor`, and an independent reviewer hunted for defects by experiment. The findings are in `term-index-2026-11-16.audits.md`. The resolutions:

- **I1. A crafted register or document could stall the builder (security N1 to N3a).** A form made only of markup characters, a scope pattern compiled to a backtracking expression, and three masking patterns could each take hours. → Every word of a form must hold a letter or a digit. Scope patterns are matched by a bounded matcher and never compiled. The masking patterns cannot rescan. Tests run hostile inputs under a time limit. - **I2. The matcher was too slow for a hook (d

- **I11. Second review of the fixes (commit 500d3cc).** `@security` and `@code-hygiene` reviewed the fix commit and found more. The matcher's work still grew with the number of forms sharing a first word, and the code-span pattern and the glob matcher were still super-linear: forms are now capped at 16 words and 32 per first word, scope lists at 64 patterns, code spans are paired in one pass, and the glob matcher makes one pass per token. A committed index file reused by the

- **I12. Third review (commit 2f5c99f).** `@security` found that the cap on forms per first word was counted per offset and so could be multiplied, and that `term-init` passed when `Projects/` was itself a symbolic link. `@code-hygiene` found the same cap problem, that plural keys were still built two ways (so a form ending in a separator could take another term's matches), and that the protocol called the project search "the detector's" while it differed in three ways. All f

Corrections to this record, found by the same review: acceptance criterion 13 said the hook exits 2 only for a broken register; it also exits 2 for a discouraged form in the file just edited. An oversized document is a `[SCOPE]` defect, not `[SCHEMA]`. A wrapped form continues after a blockquote prefix or indentation; a list marker on the next line is not skipped. No cases were added to `tests/test_init_personalization.py`; the managed-block test is in `tests/test_term_index.

- **A hook entry point under `.claude/hooks/` (F-19).** That directory is generated by agentteams. `@security` ruled that an example invoking the script under `scripts/` is acceptable, the same arrangement as the existing toolchain hook. The example's comment states the exposure. - **A bash scenario suite (F-27, C12).** The new scripts are Python, and `@code-hygiene` ruled pytest correct for them. The autosync gate's detector loop is unchanged. - **`brief.json` criteria (C16)
Under `<project>/terminology/`, where `<project>` is a research project directory under `Projects/`, at any depth:

- `terms.json` — the term register. Authored. - `term-index.json` — the manifest: register hash, generator version, and each indexed document's hash. Generated. - `index/<document path>.json` — that document's occurrences. Generated. - `glossary.md` — a reading view of the register. Generated.
All generated files are committed. They hold no timestamps and no absolute paths. Paths are POSIX and relative to the project.

```json { "schema": "researchteam-term-register", "schema_version": "1.0", "scope": {"include": ["**/*.md"], "exclude": []}, "terms": [ { "id": "occurrence-index", "label": "occurrence index", "definition": "A derived record of every place a registered term or one of its listed variants appears in the project's documents.", "variants": ["occurrence indexing"], "discouraged": ["term concordance"], "source": "project definition", "notes": "Optional." } ], "allow": [ {"term": "o

- Required per term: `id` (a lower-case slug), `label`, `definition`. Optional: `variants`, `discouraged`, `source`, `notes`, `plural` (default `true`). - An unknown key is a `[SCHEMA]` defect, so a misspelt key is not silently ignored. - `allow` records a deliberate use of a term's discouraged forms in one file, with a reason. - Limits bound the size of a register and the work of matching. They are listed in `docs/term-index-protocol.md` ("The register") and are not repeated

- A form matches whole words. A letter, a digit or a hyphen on either side prevents a match. - A form written in lower case matches without regard to case. A form containing a capital letter matches exactly. - Between the words of a form: spaces, or one line break (with a blockquote prefix or indentation on the next line), or a hyphen. Emphasis markers around a word are ignored. A match never crosses a blank line or leaves a heading. - With `plural` on, the last word also mat

`python3 scripts/check_term_index.py [project]`. Exit 0 clean, 1 defect, 2 usage or environment error. The finding codes, with which block and which are advisory, are defined in `docs/term-index-protocol.md` ("The gate") and are not repeated here. In outline: a malformed or ambiguous register, a `source` key missing from the `.bib`, an empty or unsafe scope, a stale or hand-edited index, a discouraged form used without a recorded exception, an orphaned index and a missing reg

Upstream, `tests.yml` runs `validate`, so layer 4 cannot be skipped there. A derived repository has no such workflow unless its owner adds one. There the gate is the local `validate` and the pre-compile check of Working Rule 8, both of which depend on being run.

The check goes inside `validate`, and not under `scripts/validate.d/`, because `validate.d` is repository-owned and is not synced. No other content check runs in `validate`. This one does because a stale index is a mechanical fact about committed files, like a broken fence.

paragraphs: A fleet session reported (2026-11-20) that `check_toolchain.py --write-lock` from researchteam v1.2.0 fails in several derived repositories: `researchteam/_release.py` `verify_tag` fetches the tag with `fetch --no-tags refs/tags/<tag>:refs/tags/<tag>`, which downloads the pinned repository's whole history under a fixed 300-second limit. On a slow link the fetch ran 477 seconds and failed. The report is data; the operator chose in this session's picker that this session fixes
The check needs only the annotated tag object (which carries the signature and names the commit) and the commit it peels to. It never reads a tree or a file.

- `verify_tag` fetches with `--depth=1 --filter=tree:0`. If that fetch fails (an old git, or a server without filter support), it retries once with `--depth=1` alone, then reports the error. - Every check after the fetch is unchanged: annotated tag, fetched object equals the advertised one, signature good against the release keys only, peel to a commit. - Tests for the fetch arguments, the fallback and the double failure.
